You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The pattern looks like early-to-mid 2022. CPI is high (+2.5 for both headline and core). The 2-year yield has risen sharply (+2.0 over 3m and 12m), and the 10y-2y spread has fallen sharply. The policy rate is still low relative to its 3-year average, but rising. Unemployment is low and falling. Bonds are selling off hard, with investment-grade credit weak, and equities are slightly negative.

Candidate months are March through May 2022. Looking at the z-scores against the prior 36 months (which include the 2020 near-zero rates), the policy rate at -0.5 fits roughly March 2022, when the first hike happened and the average over the prior 36 months was still around 1%. The 2y 3m change of +2.0 also fits, as the 2y rose from about 0.7% to 2.3% between December 2021 and March 2022.

Other months in 2022 fit less well. In April 2022, the policy rate was about 0.33%, still below its 36-month average. Equities were -1.5 for the 1m, which fits April (S&P -8.7%). Treasuries 7-10y at -1.5 for 1m also fits April, but the 1m for March fits less. The 12m equity return of +0.0 fits April 2022, since the 12m return was only about 0%. In March, it was about +15%, which would be above average. The VIX at +0.5 fits April. Gold at -0.5 for 1m fits April (-2%). The dollar's 3m change of +1.5 also fits April. EM equity 12m at -1.0 fits April as well.

I'll go with April 2022.
